shloka_text: रामस्य भाषितं श्रुत्वा लक्ष्मणः परवीरहा । उवाच प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यं राघवं दीप्ततेजसम् ।। 7.56.1 ।।
transliteration: rāmasya bhāṣitaṃ śrutvā lakṣmaṇaḥ paravīrahā | uvāca prāñjalirvākyaṃ rāghavaṃ dīptatejasam || 7.56.1 ||
translation: रामस्य of Rama, भाषितं words, श्रुत्वा having heard, लक्ष्मणः Lakshmana, परवीरहा destroyer of enemy heroes, उवाच spoke, प्राञ्जलिः with folded hands, वाक्यं words, राघवं to Rama, दीप्ततेजसम् of blazing splendor.
explanation: Having heard Rama's words, Lakshmana, the destroyer of enemy heroes, spoke with folded hands to the radiant Rama.
comments: Lakshmana asks how the two regained their bodies -- Rama tells that the bodiless Vasishtha, sent by Brahma to be reborn without a womb, goes to Varuna's abode, where Varuna, smitten by the apsara Urvashi who is pledged to Mitra, sheds his seed into a pot -- slighted, Mitra curses Urvashi to dwell among men as the wife of King Pururavas, ancestress of Ayus and Nahusha.

shloka_text: निक्षिप्तदेहौ काकुत्स्य कथं तौ द्विजपार्थिवौ । पुनर्देहेन संयोगं जग्मतुर्देवसम्मतौ ।। 7.56.2 ।।
transliteration: nikṣiptadehau kākutsya kathaṃ tau dvijapārthivau | punardehena saṃyogaṃ jagmaturdevasammatau || 7.56.2 ||
translation: निक्षिप्तदेहौ having cast off their bodies, काकुत्स्य O Kakutstha, कथं how, तौ those two, द्विजपार्थिवौ the Brahmin and the king, पुनः again, देहेन with a body, संयोगं union, जग्मतुः attained, देवसम्मतौ honored by the gods.
explanation: O Kakutstha, how did those two, the Brahmin and the king, who had cast off their bodies and were honored by the gods, attain union with a body again?

shloka_text: लक्ष्मणेनैवमुक्तस्तु रामश्चेक्ष्वाकुनन्दनः । प्रत्युवाच महातेजा लक्ष्मणं पुरुषर्षभः ।। 7.56.3 ।।
transliteration: lakṣmaṇenaivamuktastu rāmaścekṣvākunandanaḥ | pratyuvāca mahātejā lakṣmaṇaṃ puruṣarṣabhaḥ || 7.56.3 ||
translation: लक्ष्मणेन by Lakshmana, एवम् thus, उक्तः spoken, तु indeed, रामः Rama, च and, इक्ष्वाकुनन्दनः delight of Ikshvaku, प्रत्युवाच replied, महातेजाः greatly effulgent, लक्ष्मणम् to Lakshmana, पुरुषर्षभः best among men.
explanation: Rama, the greatly effulgent best among men and descendant of Ikshvaku, thus replied to Lakshmana who had spoken to him.

shloka_text: तौ परस्परशापेन देहावुत्सृज्य धार्मिकौ । अभूतां नृपविप्रर्षी वायुभूतौ तपोधनौ ।। 7.56.4 ।।
transliteration: tau parasparaśāpena dehāvutsṛjya dhārmikau | abhūtāṃ nṛpaviprarṣī vāyubhūtau tapodhanau || 7.56.4 ||
translation: तौ those two, परस्परशापेन by mutual curse, देहौ bodies, उत्सृज्य having abandoned, धार्मिकौ righteous ones, अभूताम् became, नृपविप्रर्षी the king and the brahmin sage, वायुभूतौ having become air, तपोधनौ whose wealth is penance.
explanation: Those two righteous ones, the king and the brahmin sage, having abandoned their bodies due to a mutual curse, became beings of air, their wealth being penance.

shloka_text: अशरीरः शरीरस्य कृते ऽन्यस्य महामुनिः । वसिष्ठः सुमहातेजा जगाम पितुरन्तिकम् ।। 7.56.5 ।।
transliteration: aśarīraḥ śarīrasya kṛte 'nyasya mahāmuniḥ | vasiṣṭhaḥ sumahātejā jagāma piturantikam || 7.56.5 ||
translation: अशरीरः bodiless, शरीरस्य for a body, कृते for the sake of, अन्यस्य another, महामुनिः the great sage, वसिष्ठः Vasishtha, सुमहातेजाः exceedingly greatly effulgent, जगाम went, पितुः of his father, अन्तिकम् to the presence.
explanation: The great sage Vasishtha, exceedingly greatly effulgent, being bodiless, went to his father's presence for the sake of another body.

shloka_text: सो ऽभिवाद्य ततः पादौ देवदेवस्य धर्मवित् । पितामहमथोवाच वायुभूत इदं वचः ।। 7.56.6 ।।
transliteration: so 'bhivādya tataḥ pādau devadevasya dharmavit | pitāmahamathovāca vāyubhūta idaṃ vacaḥ || 7.56.6 ||
translation: सः he, अभिवाद्य having saluted, ततः then, पादौ the feet, देवदेवस्य of the god of gods, धर्मवित् knower of dharma, पितामहम् to the grandfather, अथ then, उवाच spoke, वायुभूतः having become air, इदम् this, वचः word.
explanation: Then, he, the knower of dharma, having become air, saluted the feet of the god of gods, his grandfather (Brahma), and spoke these words.

shloka_text: भगवन्निमिशापेन विदेहत्वमुपागमम् । लोकनाथ महादेव अण्डजो ऽपि त्वमब्जजः ।। 7.56.7 ।।
transliteration: bhagavannimiśāpena videhatvamupāgamam | lokanātha mahādeva aṇḍajo 'pi tvamabjajaḥ || 7.56.7 ||
translation: भगवन् O Lord, निमि Nimi, शापेन by the curse, विदेहत्वम् bodiless state, उपागमम् I have attained, लोकनाथ O Lord of the worlds, महादेव O great god, अण्डजः born from an egg, अपि even, त्वम् you, अब्जजः born from a lotus.
explanation: O Lord, O Lord of the worlds, O great god, I have attained a bodiless state due to Nimi's curse, and you yourself are born from an egg and a lotus.

shloka_text: सर्वेषां देहहीनानां महद्दुःखं भविष्यति । लुप्यन्ते सर्वकार्यणि हीनदेहस्य वै प्रभो । देहस्यान्यस्य सद्भावे प्रसादं कर्तुमर्हसि ।। 7.56.8 ।।
transliteration: sarveṣāṃ dehahīnānāṃ mahadduḥkhaṃ bhaviṣyati | lupyante sarvakāryaṇi hīnadehasya vai prabho | dehasyānyasya sadbhāve prasādaṃ kartumarhasi || 7.56.8 ||
translation: सर्वेषां of all, देहहीनानां of those without a body, महद्दुःखं great sorrow, भविष्यति will be, लुप्यन्ते are destroyed, सर्वकार्यणि all actions, हीनदेहस्य of one without a body, वै indeed, प्रभो O Lord, देहस्य of a body, अन्यस्य another, सद्भावे in the existence, प्रसादं favor, कर्तुम् to do, अर्हसि you ought.
explanation: O Lord, great sorrow will befall all those without a body, as all actions are lost for one who lacks a physical form; therefore, you ought to grant the favor of another body.

shloka_text: तमुवाच ततो ब्रह्मा स्वयम्भूरमितप्रभः । मित्रावरुणजं तेज प्रविश त्वं महायशः ।। 7.56.9 ।।
transliteration: tamuvāca tato brahmā svayambhūramitaprabhaḥ | mitrāvaruṇajaṃ teja praviśa tvaṃ mahāyaśaḥ || 7.56.9 ||
translation: तम् him, उवाच said, ततो then, ब्रह्मा Brahma, स्वयम्भूः the self-born, अमितप्रभः of immeasurable splendor, मित्रावरुणजं born of Mitra and Varuna, तेज the essence, प्रविश enter, त्वं you, महायशः O greatly renowned one.
explanation: Then, Brahma, the self-born one of immeasurable splendor, said to him, "O greatly renowned one, enter the essence born of Mitra and Varuna."

shloka_text: अयोनिजस्त्वं भविता तत्रापि द्विजसत्तम । धर्मेण महता युक्तः पुनरेष्यसि मे वशम् ।। 7.56.10 ।।
transliteration: ayonijastvaṃ bhavitā tatrāpi dvijasattama | dharmeṇa mahatā yuktaḥ punareṣyasi me vaśam || 7.56.10 ||
translation: अयोनिजः not born from a womb, त्वं you, भविता will be, तत्रापि even there, द्विजसत्तम O best among twice-born, धर्मेण with righteousness, महता great, युक्तः endowed, पुनः again, एष्यसि you will come, मे my, वशम् control.
explanation: O best among twice-born, even there you will be born without a womb, and endowed with great righteousness, you will again return to my control.

shloka_text: एवमुक्तस्तु देवेन चाभिवाद्य प्रदक्षिणम् । कृत्वा पितामहं तूर्णं प्रययौ वरुणालयम् ।। 7.56.11 ।।
transliteration: evamuktastu devena cābhivādya pradakṣiṇam | kṛtvā pitāmahaṃ tūrṇaṃ prayayau varuṇālayam || 7.56.11 ||
translation: एवम् thus, उक्तः spoken, तु indeed, देवेन by the god, च and, अभिवाद्य having saluted, प्रदक्षिणम् circumambulation, कृत्वा having done, पितामहं the grandfather, तूर्णं quickly, प्रययौ went, वरुणालयम् to the abode of Varuna.
explanation: Thus spoken to by the god, and having saluted and circumambulated the grandfather Brahma, he quickly went to the abode of Varuna.

shloka_text: तमेव कालं मित्रो ऽपि वरुणत्वमकारयत् । क्षीरोदेन सहोपेतः पूज्यमानः सुरोत्तमैः ।। 7.56.12 ।।
transliteration: tameva kālaṃ mitro 'pi varuṇatvamakārayat | kṣīrodena sahopetaḥ pūjyamānaḥ surottamaiḥ || 7.56.12 ||
translation: तम् that, एव very, कालं time, मित्रो Mitra, अपि also, वरुणत्वम् the state of Varuna, अकारयत् caused to be done, क्षीरोदेन with the ocean of milk, सह with, उपेतः accompanied, पूज्यमानः being worshipped, सुरोत्तमैः by the best of gods.
explanation: At that very time, Mitra also performed the role of Varuna, accompanied by the Ocean of Milk and being worshipped by the best of gods.

shloka_text: एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु उर्वशी परमाप्सराः । यदृच्छया तमुद्देशमाययौ सखिभिर्वृता ।। 7.56.13 ।।
transliteration: etasminneva kāle tu urvaśī paramāpsarāḥ | yadṛcchayā tamuddeśamāyayau sakhibhirvṛtā || 7.56.13 ||
translation: एतस्मिन्नेव काले in that very time, तु indeed, उर्वशी Urvashi, परमाप्सराः the chief Apsara, यदृच्छया by chance, तम् उद्देशम् to that place, आययौ came, सखिभिर्वृता surrounded by friends.
explanation: At that very time, Urvashi, the foremost Apsara, arrived at that place by chance, accompanied by her friends.

shloka_text: तां दृष्ट्वा रूपसम्पन्नां क्रीडन्तीं वरुणालये । आविशत्परमो हर्षो वरुणं चोर्वशीकृते ।। 7.56.14 ।।
transliteration: tāṃ dṛṣṭvā rūpasampannāṃ krīḍantīṃ varuṇālaye | āviśatparamo harṣo varuṇaṃ corvaśīkṛte || 7.56.14 ||
translation: ताम् her, दृष्ट्वा having seen, रूपसम्पन्नाम् endowed with beauty, क्रीडन्तीम् playing, वरुणालये in Varuna's abode, आविशत् entered, परमो हर्षो great joy, वरुणम् Varuna, च and, उर्वशीकृते for Urvashi's sake.
explanation: Having seen her, beautiful and playing in Varuna's abode, great joy entered Varuna because of Urvashi.

shloka_text: स तां पद्मपलाशाक्षीं पूर्णचन्द्रनिभाननाम् । वरुणो वरयामास मैथुनायाप्सरोवराम् ।। 7.56.15 ।।
transliteration: sa tāṃ padmapalāśākṣīṃ pūrṇacandranibhānanām | varuṇo varayāmāsa maithunāyāpsarovarām || 7.56.15 ||
translation: सः he, ताम् her, पद्मपलाशाक्षीम् lotus-petal-eyed, पूर्णचन्द्रनिभाननाम् with a face like the full moon, वरुणः Varuna, वरयामास desired, मैथुनाय for union, अप्सरोवराम् the best of Apsaras.
explanation: Varuna, seeing her with lotus-petal eyes and a face like the full moon, desired her, the best of Apsaras, for union.

shloka_text: प्रत्युवाच ततः सा तु वरुणं प्राञ्जलिः स्थिता । मित्रेणाहं वृता साक्षात्पूर्वमेव सुरेश्वर ।। 7.56.16 ।।
transliteration: pratyuvāca tataḥ sā tu varuṇaṃ prāñjaliḥ sthitā | mitreṇāhaṃ vṛtā sākṣātpūrvameva sureśvara || 7.56.16 ||
translation: प्रत्युवाच replied, ततः then, सा she, तु indeed, वरुणम् to Varuna, प्राञ्जलिः स्थिता standing with folded hands, मित्रेण by Mitra, अहम् I, वृता chosen, साक्षात् directly, पूर्वम् एव already, सुरेश्वर O Lord of gods.
explanation: Then she, standing with folded hands, replied to Varuna, saying, "O Lord of gods, I have already been directly chosen by Mitra."

shloka_text: वरुणस्त्वब्रवीद्वाक्यं कन्दर्पशरपीडितः । इदं तेजः समुत्स्रक्ष्ये कुम्भे ऽस्मिन्देवनिर्मिते ।। 7.56.17 ।।
transliteration: varuṇastvabravīdvākyaṃ kandarpaśarapīḍitaḥ | idaṃ tejaḥ samutsrakṣye kumbhe 'smindevanirmite || 7.56.17 ||
translation: वरुणः Varuna, तु however, अब्रवीत् spoke, वाक्यम् words, कन्दर्पशरपीडितः tormented by the arrows of Kama, इदम् this, तेजः semen, समुत्स्रक्ष्ये I shall discharge, कुम्भे in the pot, अस्मिन् this, देवनिर्मिते made by gods.
explanation: Tormented by the arrows of Kama, Varuna then spoke, saying, "I shall discharge this semen into this pot made by the gods."

shloka_text: एवमुत्सृज्य सुश्रोणि त्वय्यहं वरवर्णिनि । कृतकामो भविष्यामि यदि नेच्छसि सङ्गमम् ।। 7.56.18 ।।
transliteration: evamutsṛjya suśroṇi tvayyahaṃ varavarṇini | kṛtakāmo bhaviṣyāmi yadi necchasi saṅgamam || 7.56.18 ||
translation: एवम् thus, उत्सृज्य abandoning (desire), सुश्रोणि O beautiful-hipped one, त्वयि in you, अहम् I, वरवर्णिनि O lady of excellent complexion, कृतकामः one whose desire is fulfilled, भविष्यामि I shall become, यदि if, न not, इच्छसि you desire, सङ्गमम् union,
explanation: O beautiful-hipped lady of excellent complexion, if you do not desire union, I shall thus abandon my desire for you and consider my wish fulfilled.

shloka_text: तस्य तल्लोकपालस्य वरुणस्य सुभाषितम् । उर्वशी परमप्रीता श्रुत्वा वाक्यमुवाच ह ।। 7.56.19 ।।
transliteration: tasya tallokapālasya varuṇasya subhāṣitam | urvaśī paramaprītā śrutvā vākyamuvāca ha || 7.56.19 ||
translation: तस्य his, तत् that, लोकपालस्य of the protector of the world, वरुणस्य of Varuna, सुभाषितम् well-spoken word, उर्वशी Urvashi, परमप्रीता extremely pleased, श्रुत्वा having heard, वाक्यम् words, उवाच ह spoke indeed,
explanation: Having heard those well-spoken words of Varuna, the protector of the world, Urvashi was extremely pleased and spoke.

shloka_text: काममेतद्भवत्वेवं हृदयं मे त्वयि स्थितम् । भावश्चाप्यधिकस्तुभ्यं देहो मित्रस्य तु प्रभो ।। 7.56.20 ।।
transliteration: kāmametadbhavatvevaṃ hṛdayaṃ me tvayi sthitam | bhāvaścāpyadhikastubhyaṃ deho mitrasya tu prabho || 7.56.20 ||
translation: कामम् indeed, एतत् this, भवतु let it be, एवम् thus, हृदयम् heart, मे my, त्वयि in you, स्थितम् situated, भावः च अपि and also feeling, अधिकः great, तुभ्यम् for you, देहः body, मित्रस्य of Mitra, तु but, प्रभो O lord,
explanation: O lord, let it be so; my heart is indeed fixed on you, and my affection for you is great, but my body belongs to Mitra.

shloka_text: उर्वश्या एवमुक्तस्तु रेतस्तन्महदद्भुतम् । ज्वलदग्निशिखाप्रख्यं तस्मिन्कुम्भे ह्यपासृजत् ।। 7.56.21 ।।
transliteration: urvaśyā evamuktastu retastanmahadadbhutam | jvaladagniśikhāprakhyaṃ tasminkumbhe hyapāsṛjat || 7.56.21 ||
translation: उर्वश्या by Urvashi, एवम् thus, उक्तः तु having been spoken to, indeed, रेतः semen, तत् that, महत् great, अद्भुतम् wonderful, ज्वलत् burning, अग्निशिखा flame of fire, प्रख्यम् resembling, तस्मिन् in that, कुम्भे pot, हि indeed, अपासृजत् he discharged,
explanation: Thus addressed by Urvashi, he indeed discharged that great and wonderful semen, resembling a burning flame of fire, into that pot.

shloka_text: उर्वशी त्वगमत्तत्र मित्रो वै यत्र देवता । तां तु मित्रः सुसङ्क्रम्य उर्वशीमिदमब्रवीत् ।। 7.56.22 ।।
transliteration: urvaśī tvagamattatra mitro vai yatra devatā | tāṃ tu mitraḥ susaṅkramya urvaśīmidamabravīt || 7.56.22 ||
translation: उर्वशी Urvashi, तु but, अगमत् went, तत्र there, मित्रः Mitra, वै indeed, यत्र where, देवता the deity, ताम् her, तु but, मित्रः Mitra, सुसङ्क्रम्य having approached well, उर्वशीम् to Urvashi, इदम् this, अब्रवीत् spoke,
explanation: But Urvashi went to the place where the deity Mitra was, and Mitra, having approached her, spoke these words to Urvashi.

shloka_text: मया निमन्त्रिता पूर्वं कस्मात्त्वमवसर्जिता । पतिमन्यं वृतवती तस्मात्त्वं दुष्टचारिणी ।। 7.56.23 ।।
transliteration: mayā nimantritā pūrvaṃ kasmāttvamavasarjitā | patimanyaṃ vṛtavatī tasmāttvaṃ duṣṭacāriṇī || 7.56.23 ||
translation: मया by me, निमन्त्रिता invited, पूर्वम् previously, कस्मात् why, त्वम् you, अवसर्जिता abandoned, पतिम् husband, अन्यम् another, वृतवती chosen, तस्मात् therefore, त्वम् you, दुष्टचारिणी ill-behaved woman.
explanation: Why did you abandon me, whom I had previously invited, and choose another husband; therefore, you are an ill-behaved woman.

shloka_text: अनेन दुष्कृतेन त्वं मत्क्रोधकलुषीकृता । मनुष्यलोकमास्थाय कञ्चित्कालं निवत्स्यसि ।। 7.56.24 ।।
transliteration: anena duṣkṛtena tvaṃ matkrodhakaluṣīkṛtā | manuṣyalokamāsthāya kañcitkālaṃ nivatsyasi || 7.56.24 ||
translation: अनेन by this, दुष्कृतेन misdeed, त्वम् you, मत्क्रोधकलुषीकृता sullied by my wrath, मनुष्यलोकम् the human world, आस्थाय having resorted to, कञ्चित्कालम् for some time, निवत्स्यसि you will reside.
explanation: Due to this misdeed, you, sullied by my wrath, will reside in the human world for some time.

shloka_text: बुधस्य पुत्रो राजर्षिः काशीराजः पुरूरवाः । तमद्य गच्छ दुर्बुद्धे स ते भर्ता भविष्यति ।। 7.56.25 ।।
transliteration: budhasya putro rājarṣiḥ kāśīrājaḥ purūravāḥ | tamadya gaccha durbuddhe sa te bhartā bhaviṣyati || 7.56.25 ||
translation: बुधस्य of Budha, पुत्रः son, राजर्षिः royal sage, काशीराजः king of Kashi, पुरूरवाः Pururavas, तम् him, अद्य today, गच्छ go, दुर्बुद्धे O ill-minded one, सः he, ते your, भर्ता husband, भविष्यति will be.
explanation: Go today to Pururavas, the royal sage, son of Budha and king of Kashi, O ill-minded one, for he will be your husband.

shloka_text: ततः सा शापदोषेण पुरूरवसमभ्यगात् । प्रतियाते पुरूरवं बुधस्यात्मजमौरसम् ।। 7.56.26 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ sā śāpadoṣeṇa purūravasamabhyagāt | pratiyāte purūravaṃ budhasyātmajamaurasam || 7.56.26 ||
translation: ततः then, सा she, शापदोषेण by the effect of the curse, पुरूरवसम् to Pururavas, अभ्यगात् went, प्रतियाते to the one who had returned, पुरूरवम् Pururavas, बुधस्य of Budha, आत्मजम् son, औरसम् legitimate.
explanation: Then she, by the effect of the curse, went to Pururavas, the legitimate son of Budha, who had returned.

shloka_text: तस्य जज्ञे ततः श्रीमानायुः पुत्रो महाबलः । नहुषो यस्य पुत्रस्तु बभूवेन्द्रसमद्युतिः ।। 7.56.27 ।।
transliteration: tasya jajñe tataḥ śrīmānāyuḥ putro mahābalaḥ | nahuṣo yasya putrastu babhūvendrasamadyutiḥ || 7.56.27 ||
translation: तस्य to him, जज्ञे was born, ततः then, श्रीमान् glorious, आयुः Ayus, पुत्रः son, महाबलः very powerful, नहुषः Nahusha, यस्य whose, पुत्रस्तु son, however, बभूव became, इन्द्रसमद्युतिः having splendor equal to Indra.
explanation: Then to him was born a glorious and very powerful son named Ayus, whose son, Nahusha, became one with splendor equal to Indra.

shloka_text: वज्रमुत्सृज्य वृत्राय भ्रान्ते ऽथ त्रिदिवेश्वरे । शतं वर्षसहस्राणि येनेन्द्रत्वं प्रशासितम् ।। 7.56.28 ।।
transliteration: vajramutsṛjya vṛtrāya bhrānte 'tha tridiveśvare | śataṃ varṣasahasrāṇi yenendratvaṃ praśāsitam || 7.56.28 ||
translation: वज्रम् thunderbolt, उत्सृज्य having cast, वृत्राय at Vritra, भ्रान्ते having erred, अथ then, त्रिदिवेश्वरे when the lord of the three heavens (Indra), शतम् a hundred, वर्षसहस्राणि thousands of years, येन by whom, इन्द्रत्वम् the position of Indra, प्रशासितम् was ruled
explanation: This refers to the one who ruled as Indra for a hundred thousand years when the actual Indra was agitated after casting his thunderbolt at Vritra.

shloka_text: सा तेन शापेन जगाम भूमिं तदोर्वशी चारुदती सुनेत्रा । बहूनि वर्षाण्यवसच्च सुभ्रूः शापक्षयादिन्द्रसदो ययौ च ।। 7.56.29 ।।
transliteration: sā tena śāpena jagāma bhūmiṃ tadorvaśī cārudatī sunetrā | bahūni varṣāṇyavasacca subhrūḥ śāpakṣayādindrasado yayau ca || 7.56.29 ||
translation: सा she, तेन by that, शापेन curse, जगाम went, भूमिम् to the earth, तदा then, उर्वशी Urvashi, चारुदती having beautiful teeth, सुनेत्रा having beautiful eyes, बहूनि many, वर्षाणि years, अवसत् resided, च and, सुभ्रूः having beautiful eyebrows, शापक्षयात् from the end of the curse, इन्द्रसदः to Indra's assembly, ययौ went, च and
explanation: That Urvashi, with beautiful teeth, eyes, and eyebrows, then went to the earth due to that curse, resided there for many years, and returned to Indra's assembly upon the curse's expiration. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे षट्पञ्चाशः सर्गः ।। 56 ।। Thus ends the fifty-sixth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
